title: LG lands multibillion dollar deal to cool North American AI data centers
source_used: Korea JoongAng Daily (pool link, fetched text); cross-checked against the joint LG and AIR press release on PR Newswire, 5 Oct 2026
key_facts: LG Electronics' US subsidiary said on Monday 5 Oct 2026 that it recently signed a long-term supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts (AIR), a North American infrastructure platform company.
LG will supply chillers and other cooling equipment in phases for AI data centers totaling 5 gigawatts of capacity in the US and Canada; the press release says more than 5 gigawatts.
The contract value was not disclosed, but an LG spokesperson said it was worth several trillion won, or several billion dollars.
AIR designs and builds data centers in the US and Canada and counts major data center operators worldwide as clients.

Cooling is one of the main constraints on building AI data centers because AI chips use far more power and give off far more heat than conventional servers; chillers are a central piece of cooling equipment.
LG and AIR are discussing extending the supply to coolant distribution units, which manage the flow of coolant in liquid cooling.
LG's AI data center cooling orders topped 600 billion won ($446.4 million) in the first half of 2026, and it expects cumulative orders of several trillion won by year-end.
quote_evidence: LG Electronics will supply chillers for 5 gigawatts of AI data center capacity under a long-term agreement with U.S.-based AIR Control Concept.
The contract value was not disclosed, but an LG Electronics spokesperson said it was worth several trillion won, or several billion dollars.
Cooling has become one of the main constraints in building AI data centers.
why_it_matters_hint: Heat is a main limit on building AI data centers, and a 5-gigawatt, multi-year chiller supply gives builders a large, long-term source of cooling equipment.
notes: Both parties are quoted in the joint release (AIR CEO Brad Hobbs; LG's James Lee), so the deal is confirmed. The value comes from an LG spokesperson to Korea JoongAng Daily and is not in the release. The Korean article spells the partner AIR Control Concept; the release says AIR Control Concepts.
